gap: No result ChatGPT got states that a cellular solar camera's built-in lithium battery stops taking a charge from the solar panel below 0 °C (32 °F). In a freezing winter the camera runs on battery alone, however much sun the panel gets.
standout_why: I compared six pages. Two were cited: Buffalo Alarm and Reolink's 4G solar guide. Four were not: SecurityCamHQ, SmartHomeExplorer, Reolink's solar buying guide and Reolink's cellular store listing. Reolink's solar guide says only that cold 'reduces the effective runtime' and that panel output falls with the winter sun angle. SecurityCamHQ says the Go PT Ultra's 'large battery provides a buffer for cloudy weeks' and that the panel needs snow clearing. Buffalo Alarm, Reolink's 4G guide and SmartHomeExplorer say nothing about charging in the cold. None of the six says charging stops at 0 °C. None names Reolink's Solar Panel 2S, the add-on panel with its own battery that keeps powering the camera down to -20 °C. Reolink's 4G guide already lists the Go PT Ultra's US LTE bands and the included SIM's carriers. So the carrier and SIM details below are only partly new.
decides: The usual buyers are remote land, farms and cabins, which are often unattended through freezing winters. For them, 'solar keeps it running forever' is false whenever daytime temperatures stay below 0 °C, and the battery must last the whole cold spell. That favours the larger battery: eufy S330 9,400 mAh against Go PT Ultra 21.6 Wh (about 5,800 mAh at a 3.7 V nominal voltage, my conversion). With Reolink, it points to the Solar Panel 2S, but Reolink's 2S pages don't list the Go PT Ultra as compatible, so check before buying. A separate point: if the shopper wants to use their own Verizon SIM in a Reolink, Reolink recommends only T-Mobile prepaid data-only SIMs or Mint and FreedomPop SIMs. A Verizon SIM must be tested in the camera first.

findings.product: general (all Reolink battery-powered cameras, incl. Go PT Ultra)
findings.label: Battery charging floor
findings.note: Maker's words: 'Ensure the environment temperature is above 0°C. The camera's built-in lithium battery cannot charge properly when the temperature is below 0°C.' Applies to: 'All Reolink Battery-powered cameras.' The page shows no date other than the 2026 copyright footer.

findings.product: Reolink Solar Panel (3 W), Solar Panel 2 (6 W), Solar Panel 3 (12 W)
findings.label: Solar charging temperature range
findings.value: 0 °C to 45 °C (32 °F to 113 °F); charging pauses below 0 °C and resumes on its own when it warms up
findings.note: Maker's words: 'Charging may temporarily stop when the current temperature is below 0°C to protect the lithium battery.' The 6 W Solar Panel 2 is the panel Reolink pairs with the Go PT Ultra.

findings.label: Cold-weather behaviour of the panel's built-in battery
findings.value: 5,900 mAh / 42.48 Wh built-in battery; recharges from -10 °C to +58 °C; between 0 °C and -20 °C it powers the camera directly instead of charging it
findings.note: Operating range -20 °C to +58 °C. Applies to 'All Reolink battery-powered cameras except Reolink Argus, Keen, and Reolink Doorbell (Battery)'. Neither this article nor the US product page (https://reolink.com/us/product/reolink-solar-panel-2s/, read 2026-11-13) names the Go PT Ultra or any 4G model. The product page gives the operating range as -10 °C to 50 °C, which conflicts with this article.

findings.label: Operating temperature
findings.source_title: Reolink Go PT Ultra (US product page)
findings.note: The camera keeps running from -10 °C to 0 °C but, per the Reolink support article above, will not charge in that range. Battery is 21.6 Wh; panel is the 6 W Solar Panel 2.

findings.label: US carriers for a third-party SIM
findings.value: Carrier table lists T-Mobile (Prepaid Data Only), AT&T (Prepaid Data Only), FreedomPop and Mint; Verizon is not listed
findings.source_title: Reolink Go PT Ultra (US product page)
findings.note: The same page says the included Reolink SIM connects to the strongest of AT&T, Verizon or T-Mobile. Verizon therefore works through Reolink's own SIM but is not listed for a SIM the buyer supplies. US bands: LTE FDD B2/B4/B5/B12/B13/B14/B66/B71.

findings.product: Reolink Go series (Go, Go PT, Go Plus, Go PT Ultra and others)
findings.label: Own-SIM guidance for the US
findings.value: Recommends a T-Mobile prepaid data-only SIM; 4G/3G only, no 5G; a Verizon SIM must be tested first
findings.source_title: How to Choose SIM Card in the United States
findings.note: Maker's words: 'If you happen to have a Verizon SIM card on hand, we recommend testing it with your camera.' Mint and FreedomPop (the AT&T-based option) are listed as compatible virtual SIMs.

findings.product: eufy 4G LTE Starlight Camera (eufy's earlier 4G solar camera)
findings.label: Charging temperature range
findings.value: 0 °C (32 °F) to 45 °C (113 °F); outside that range 'the camera cannot be charged'
findings.note: This is eufy's own statement for its 4G solar camera, not for the S330. It shows eufy uses the same lithium charging floor as Reolink. I found no eufy statement giving the S330's charging range.

findings.value: 9,400 mAh battery; switches to 4G when the Wi-Fi signal is lost; included 3-in-1 SIM
